If you ever want to truly grasp travel in space, KSP is what you need to play. I thought I had a good understanding of what it meant to launch rockets, but I clearly knew nothing. EVERYTHING is in motion! You have to go fast not to fall, not just up. If you thought it was ridiculous that that one Mars rover crashed because the scientists forgot to convert metric to imperial units, well you just wait and see the stupid, clumsy mistakes you make putting together a rocket. One of my core gaming memories came from KSP years ago from the free to play demo. The first time you forget to add a parachute for the return vehicle (and it will happen), your heart will sink knowing there is absolutely nothing you can do as your little buddies hurtle inevitably towards the ground. It drew me in.

One of my greatest achievements in any game also came from KSP. I successfully landed a Kerbal on the Mun and ran him around on the soil, then bringing him back home safely, without the use of any mods and without looking up any guides to find ideal launch windows and turning arcs, and how fast my ship should be travelling through the different levels of atmosphere.
You'll spend hours and hours and days and weeks building different rockets in different configurations and different timings, then docking them and making stations and sending out remote probes.... all without ever beginning to touch mods. And there are TONS of them. From ones that launch things for you and bring you to whatever height above the surface you want, but also ones that only add an extra part or two, or ones that turn it into a form of war simulator. Definitely worth buying. Absolutely worth trying the free trial that came out nearly featureless years ago, if there is still one available. Featureless as compared to current I mean, and that thing still was a blast.

After playing for a couple years I finally started adding some mods to freshen up the experience and although it adds a bunch to the game (a lot of them are amazing!), the 2 unmodded years made the coming modded years so great. I've never played a game that made me feel a sense of pride and achievement like KSP. That first mun landing, my first trip to Duna, my first landing on Duna, my 1st rescue mission to Duna, my 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th rescue missions to Duna... Duna is a bitch of a planet at times.
